text: When designing or proposing Wagtail block types, especially UnionBlock-based choice fields, avoid duplicating shared fields or requiring a custom StructValue for common use cases: define shared fields on a common StructBlock base class that union members subclass, push type-specific rendering into the chosen constituent block's get_context or template, and prefer a unified type hierarchy over parallel implementations.
reason: Shared base classes reduce field duplication, constituent-block logic keeps common UnionBlock use cases simple without custom StructValue, unified hierarchies simplify tooling such as migrations and comments, and proposals must explicitly address field duplication when comparing StructBlock and UnionBlock ergonomics.
scope: Wagtail block type / UnionBlock API design
common_pattern: Designing Wagtail block-type APIs to reduce duplication and unnecessary custom value handling by sharing fields through common base block types, pushing type-specific rendering into constituent blocks, and preferring unified type hierarchies over parallel implementations.

text: In Wagtail image APIs and configuration, avoid per-format boolean flags/properties such as `is_svg` or `WAGTAILIMAGES_ALLOW_SVG`. Instead use a generic, extensible collection/setting/property keyed by canonical lowercase format (for example `WAGTAILIMAGES_ALLOWED_FORMATS` or `image.is.<format>`), support a wildcard value like `'*'` to allow any format, and derive format-specific behavior from membership in that collection. When identifying an image's format, prefer the canonical `Image.format` over the raw file extension, since aliases such as `.jpg` and `.jpeg` map to the same format.
reason: Keeps the API extensible for new image formats, avoids one-off flags and extension alias lists, and provides a single consistent place to configure or check allowed formats in Wagtail.
common_pattern: Avoid format-specific boolean flags/properties in Wagtail image APIs and configuration; centralize format handling in generic, extensible collections/settings/properties, with canonical format values and wildcard support.

text: Design Wagtail viewsets for reuse across models: expose a base viewset class with no model-specific workflow hardcoded, register one endpoint per model (mirroring the existing read API), and have `wagtail_hooks.py` registration functions (e.g. `register_snippet`) accept either the model class or its ViewSet class as the first positional argument and dispatch on the argument type, allowing both model-first and ViewSet-first registration.
reason: Lets pages, snippets, ModelAdmin, and other models reuse the same mechanism instead of a Page-only (or model-specific) endpoint, and supports migration toward ViewSet-centric registration without breaking existing model-first calls (making the `viewset=` keyword redundant).
common_pattern: Design of a reusable, extensible Wagtail admin/API viewset registration architecture: base classes without model-specific workflow, one endpoint per model, optional views that can be disabled, and registration functions that accept either a model or a ViewSet class.

text: In Wagtail admin viewsets (e.g. `SnippetViewSet`), model optional views as overridable `{foo}_view_class` (or `{foo}_view`) attributes and have `get_urlpatterns()` conditionally register a view's URLs only when the attribute is present; to disable a view or action, prefer denying access through a custom PermissionHelper (e.g. return False) instead of removing/nullifying view classes or URL patterns, and ensure the admin UI gracefully handles disabled/absent views without rendering links or actions that assume they exist.
reason: Supports partial registration (e.g. CRUD without chooser) without dead URL routes, while permission-level denial integrates with the existing authorization framework, avoids UI inconsistencies, and keeps disabled admin functionality safe and understandable.
scope: Wagtail admin viewsets (`SnippetViewSet`) / optional views, URL registration & permissions
common_pattern: Disabling optional Wagtail admin views/actions should be handled at the permission-checking level rather than by removing view classes or URL patterns, and the admin UI must gracefully handle disabled or absent views.

text: Model each concurrent editing session as its own entity with a unique session ID (e.g. UUID) stored as an individual database row, rather than as a unique `(object, user)` association or a shared singleton row. Use the session ID for session-specific API endpoints and the user ID for authorization/filtering; perform any user-level aggregation or deduplication only in query/UI layers. For optimistic concurrency, use a version token that changes on every update (timestamp, UUID, or counter) rather than relying on a stable record ID.
reason: Combines the session-record and version-token requirements needed to avoid collapsing multiple tabs/sessions or missing in-place updates.
common_pattern: Concurrency-safe state modeling: avoid shared/singleton mutable records for concurrent clients and avoid relying on stable identifiers alone to detect stale updates.
